page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 16 burstable virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at up to 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 128 GB of DDR5 memory rated at 7 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. No local disk storage is bundled, relying strictly on remote EBS storage, and hardware accelerators are absent with zero GPUs configured. Networking provides a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results show strong single-thread efficiency and consistent multi-core throughput across compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2161.0, placing in the top quartile, complemented by top-tier text processing performance at 2930.0. Cryptographic and compression tasks also performed well, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.04 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.41 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory bandwidth registered at 136.43 GB/sec for reads and 66.04 GB/sec for writes. Multi-core compute benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core at 17340.84 and PassMark CPU at 29208.35, fell within middle-tier distribution, reflecting burstable resource allocation characteristics.

The r8i-flex.4xlarge provides a cost-effective memory footprint for workloads that demand significant memory capacity without continuously saturating all 16 virtual CPUs. Because compute allocation is burstable, sustained full-core processing may encounter throttling compared to non-flex tiers, and the absence of local NVMe storage necessitates network-attached storage planning. The system is well matched for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and non-relational database engines with large working sets, data extraction pipelines, and small model language inference.
